skill.name: super-swarm-spark

content.value_statement: Large development plans are hard to execute across many related tasks. This skill turns a plan into parallel Sparky assignments and guides final integration.
actual_capabilities: Parses markdown plan files for task sections and optional task subsets.
Builds context packs with canonical paths, related tasks, naming rules, and validation notes.
Schedules up to 12 Sparky subagents in a rolling pool.
Validates each completion, updates plan status, and retries or escalates failures.
Performs a final integration pass with tests and conflict cleanup.
limitations: Requires a structured markdown plan with clear task sections and file paths.
Depends on the availability of a compatible Sparky subagent role.
Parallel work can create merge conflicts or duplicated edits that require review.
Does not replace human judgment for architecture, security, or release approval.

use_cases.title: Execute Large Feature Plans
use_cases.description: Break a detailed implementation plan into parallel assignments and keep task progress moving.

use_cases.title: Accelerate Backlog Cleanup
use_cases.description: Run selected maintenance tasks from a plan while preserving canonical file paths and naming rules.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Validation Work
use_cases.description: Assign implementation and verification tasks, then review completion logs and final test results.

prompt_templates.title: Run A Full Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the whole plan is ready for parallel execution.

prompt_templates.title: Run Selected Tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when only specific task IDs should be assigned.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Shared Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Use super-swarm-spark with ./plans/ui-plan.md. Preserve canonical paths and stop any subagent that needs unlisted files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when several tasks may touch the same files.

prompt_templates.title: Recover And Integrate
prompt_templates.prompt: Use super-swarm-spark for ./plans/api-plan.md. Revalidate completed tasks, resolve integration conflicts, run tests, and update the execution summary.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after parallel work needs final review and integration.

output_examples.input: Run the full checkout migration plan.
output: Assigned eight tasks with a rolling pool of Sparky subagents.
Validated each completed task against its acceptance criteria.
Updated the plan file and reported integration fixes.

output_examples.input: Run only tasks T3 and T7 from the profile plan.
output: Filtered the plan to the requested task IDs.
Prepared context packs with canonical file paths.
Returned task summaries, validation notes, and blockers.

output_examples.input: Finish integration after the subagents complete.
output: Reviewed completed task outputs for conflicts and gaps.
Ran the planned validation checks where feasible.
Prepared a concise execution summary for review.

best_practices: Provide explicit file paths, acceptance criteria, and validation commands in the plan.
Keep task scopes small enough for independent subagents to finish and report clearly.
Review final integration changes before merging or releasing.
anti_patterns: Running the skill on vague plans that lack task IDs or file targets.
Ignoring conflicts between parallel edits after subagents finish.
Using it for security-sensitive changes without manual review.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It coordinates Sparky subagents to execute markdown development plans in parallel.

faq.question: Does it need a plan file?
faq.answer: Yes. It expects a structured markdown plan with clear task sections.

faq.question: Can it run only some tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. The user can provide specific task IDs to filter the plan.

faq.question: How many subagents can it use?
faq.answer: Its scheduling policy uses up to 12 active Sparky subagents.

faq.question: Does it commit changes?
faq.answer: The task template asks subagents to commit only their own files and never push.

faq.question: Should humans review the result?
faq.answer: Yes. Parallel edits and final integration should be reviewed before release.
